Form 40 baseline TY2017-2025. OWN BASE (start_point 0, ob_* shares): AL builds its own income concept, not federal AGI. SS and UI FULLY EXEMPT (no provisional test). ob_class_floor 0 -- AL has no PA-style class loss ring-fence and is MORE generous than federal on capital losses (entire loss deductible, no $3k cap). FULL UNCAPPED federal income tax deduction (constitutional, Amendment 225): base = 1040 line 22 + NIIT ADDED BACK - (EITC + ACTC + refundable AOC), so AL subtracts the ACTC where MO does not and does NOT subtract net PTC where MO does -- hence the fed_tax_ded_less_* flags are per-credit. NO EXEMPTIONS -- AR grants personal CREDITS instead (exempt_credit machinery): $26 through TY2019 and $29 from TY2020 (the widely-quoted $26 is right only through 2019; it is CONDITIONALLY indexed off a CY2001 $20 base and only steps when a revenue trigger fires, which is why it moved once in nine years). 50% of net LONG-TERM capital gain excluded (short-term fully taxable, hence the new ob_st_gains_share); $6,000 retirement exemption per taxpayer, flat, never indexed, NO age test on the employer-plan branch; SS fully exempt; UI FLIPS THREE TIMES (exempt 2017, taxable 2018-19, exempt 2020-21, taxable 2022+). IT-540 baseline TY2017-2025. THE ENCODING SUBTLETY THAT DOMINATES THIS STATE is where the exemption comes off. Louisiana does NOT subtract the combined personal exemption-standard deduction before applying the brackets: R.S. 47:32(A)(1)/294/295(B), as LDR states them in RIB 21-032 fn.5, require it to be 'deducted from the lowest tax bracket first and then the remaining brackets in increasing order', i.e. tax = sched(tax table income) - sched(E) with bracket bounds anchored to UNREDUCED income. ALL 43,008 CELLS of the published TY2017-TY2024 tax tables reproduce exactly under that rule and NOT under sched(TTI - E) -- a TY2021 single filer with one exemption and 27,625 of TTI owes 765, where the naive form gives 675 (new st_ord.exempt_from_bottom; pinned by LA-1). One consequence: where E exceeds the first bracket (joint/HoH with several exemptions) the excess is relieved at the SECOND bracket rate. THREE RATE REGIMES: 2/4/6% through TY2021 alongside a CONSTITUTIONALLY MANDATED, UNCAPPED federal income tax deduction; 1.85/3.50/4.25% for TY2022-24 after Act 395 of 2021 traded that deduction for lower rates (contingent on Amendment No. 2, ratified 2021-11-13 223,269 to 189,973 -- note the amendment only made the deduction PERMISSIVE and set a 4.75% rate ceiling; the repeal was STATUTORY); and a FLAT 3% from TY2025 under Act 11 of the 2024 Third E.S., verified from R.S. 47:32(A) and IT-540 line 11 ('Multiply Line 10 by .03') -- no TY2025 tax table exists. Bracket bounds NEVER MOVED and were never indexed: 12,500/50,000 for single, MFS AND HoH, doubled for MFJ/QSS. BIGGEST CORRECTION TO THE SECONDARY LITERATURE: the EXCESS FEDERAL ITEMIZED DEDUCTION was NOT repealed in 2022, it was NARROWED to medical and dental only (R.S. 47:293(3)), and the narrowed version is still on the TY2025 return -- line 8A, the itemized total, is collected but UNUSED in the arithmetic from TY2022 (new st_ded.item_less_fed_std; pinned by LA-8a/8b). It points at the FEDERAL standard deduction rather than printing its own amounts, so federal std-deduction reforms reach Louisiana through that line. HoH IS A HYBRID and easy to get wrong: the JOINT exemption base of 9,000 with add-ons starting after ONE exemption, but the SINGLE brackets (verified against 1,344 HoH table cells per year; pinned by LA-4). Exemption structure through TY2024: 4,500 S/MFS, 9,000 MFJ/QSS/HoH, plus 1,000 per exemption beyond the first (S/MFS/HoH) or beyond the second (MFJ/QSS) -- which works out to 1,000 per dependant, per 65+ taxpayer and per blind taxpayer in every status.
